title: Cosori air fryer recall: the 2023 model list and the Pro II
description: The February 23, 2023 CPSC and Health Canada notices name specific Cosori air fryer model numbers. The COSORI Pro II card uses the CS358-AF series, which is not in those lists.
catalogue: The COSORI Pro II card’s model line reads CS358-AF series. CS358-AF is not among the model numbers copied from the notices below.

notices.title: Two Million COSORI Air Fryers Recalled by Atekcity Due to Fire and Burn Hazards
notices.says: The CPSC notice says this recall involves Cosori air fryers with the model numbers listed below. It says the brand name Cosori is on the front of each unit, the model number is printed on the bottom label and in the user manual, and the units are 3.7 and 5.8 quart, sold in black, gray, white, blue, or red.
notices.howToCheck: The notice says to read the model number on the bottom label of the unit and in the user manual.
notices.remedy: The notice tells owners to stop using the recalled air fryers and contact Cosori for a free replacement air fryer or another Cosori product. It says registration asks for contact information and photos of the unit with the cord cut, and that no receipt is needed.
notices.modelsLabel: Model numbers in the CPSC notice

notices.title: Certain models of Cosori-branded Air Fryers recalled due to potential fire hazard
notices.says: The Health Canada notice, updated 2023-02-23, says the recall involves certain Cosori-branded air fryers and describes a fire hazard. It says the notice is a joint recall with the CPSC. Its model column also uses the shorter names CO137, CO158, CP137, CP158, CP258, and CS158.
notices.howToCheck: The notice says the model number is on the bottom label and in the user manual, and the batch number is on the bottom of the unit or at the back below the rear exhaust vent.
notices.remedy: The notice tells owners to stop using the recalled products immediately and contact Cosori for a replacement unit.
notices.modelsLabel: Model numbers in the Health Canada notice

title: Ninja Foodi OP300 and TenderCrisp lid notices
description: The May 1, 2025 CPSC notice names Ninja Foodi OP300-series pressure cookers. The Health Canada notice names TenderCrisp pressure-cooking lids. The DT201C oven and FN101 Crispi cards are not those model numbers.
catalogue: The Foodi oven card’s model line reads DT201C. The Crispi card’s model line reads FN101. Neither string is in the model lists copied below.

notices.title: SharkNinja Recalls Foodi Multi-Function Pressure Cookers Due to Burn Hazard
notices.says: The CPSC notice says the recall involves all Ninja Foodi OP300 Series Multi-Function Pressure Cookers, with pressure cooking and air frying, sold in black with a 6.5-quart capacity. It says Ninja is printed on the front and on the product label. It says an extra code after the model number is not part of the model designation, and gives the example that a unit labeled OP301 I07 is a model OP301. It also includes OP300-series replacement pressure-cooker lids bought as a separate part.
notices.howToCheck: The notice says the model numbers are printed on a label on the side of the cooker.
notices.remedy: The notice tells owners to stop using the pressure-cooking function and contact SharkNinja for a free replacement lid. It says the air frying and other functions can still be used.
notices.modelsLabel: Model numbers in the CPSC notice

notices.title: Ninja Foodi TenderCrisp pressure-cooking lid recalled due to potential burn hazard
notices.says: The Health Canada notice says the recall involves the pressure-cooking lid on Ninja Foodi TenderCrisp multi-cookers, including replacement pressure-cooking lids bought separately from SharkNinja. It says the cookers have a 6.5-quart chamber and the brand name Ninja is on the front of the hinged lid. It says other functions, such as air crisping, are not part of this recall.
notices.howToCheck: The notice says the model number is on the rating label on the back of the unit, near the power cord.
notices.remedy: The notice tells owners to stop using the pressure-cooking function, dispose of the pressure-cooking lid so it cannot be used, and contact SharkNinja to confirm that disposal and arrange a replacement lid.
notices.modelsLabel: Model numbers in the Health Canada notice

title: Anker power bank recalls: official model numbers
description: CPSC and Health Canada power-bank notices name specific Anker model numbers, and some of those notices cover only certain serial numbers. A1289 is not one of those model numbers.
catalogue: The catalogue power bank is model A1289, the Anker 737 PowerCore 24K. A1289 is not among the model numbers copied from the notices below.

notices.title: Anker Power Banks Recalled Due to Fire and Burn Hazards
notices.says: The CPSC notice says this recall involves Anker PowerCore 10000 power banks with model number A1263. It says Anker is engraved on the front, and the model number and serial number are printed on the bottom. It says only A1263 units sold in the U.S. with qualifying serial numbers are included.
notices.howToCheck: The notice says to read model A1263 and the serial number on the bottom, then check that serial number at anker.com/product-recalls.
notices.remedy: The notice tells owners to stop using a recalled power bank and contact Anker for a free replacement. It says the registration asks for a photo showing the model number, serial number, the owner’s name, the date, and the word recalled written on the unit. It also says not to put the lithium-ion battery in household trash or ordinary recycling.
notices.modelsLabel: Model number in this CPSC notice

notices.title: Anker Power Banks Recalled Due to Fire and Burn Hazards
notices.says: The CPSC notice says this recall involves Anker power banks with model numbers A1642, A1647, and A1652. It says Anker is engraved on the front and the model number is on the back.
notices.howToCheck: The notice says the model number is on the back of the power bank.
notices.remedy: The notice tells owners to stop using the recalled power banks and contact Anker for a free replacement, registering at anker.com/product-recalls. It says to dispose of the lithium-ion batteries under local rules.
notices.modelsLabel: Model numbers in this CPSC notice

notices.title: Fantasia Trading Recalls Anker Power Banks Due to Fire Hazard
notices.says: The CPSC notice says this recall involves Anker 535 mobile power banks, PowerCore 20K, with model number A1366. It says Anker is engraved on the front and A1366 is on the back.
notices.howToCheck: The notice says the model number A1366 is on the back of the power bank.
notices.remedy: The notice tells owners to stop using the recalled power banks and contact Fantasia Trading for a full refund and for its instructions on disposing of the lithium-ion batteries.
notices.modelsLabel: Model number in this CPSC notice

notices.title: Anker Power Bank A1647 and Anker Zolo Power Banks A1681 and A1689 recalled due to fire hazard
notices.says: The Health Canada notice says certain units of Anker Power Bank A1647 and Anker Zolo power banks A1681 and A1689 are recalled for a fire hazard. It says affected units are identified by serial number, and that serial numbers of affected products do not contain the letters O or I.
notices.howToCheck: The notice says the serial number is printed on the side or the back, and to compare it with the list at anker.com/ca/rc2506.
notices.remedy: The notice tells owners to stop using the recalled units and contact Anker for a free replacement or a voucher. It says to dispose of the lithium-ion battery so it cannot be used, using the municipality’s instructions, and not to put it in household garbage.
notices.modelsLabel: Model numbers in this Health Canada notice

notices.title: Anker 334 MagGo Battery (PowerCore 10K), model A1642, recalled due to potential fire hazard
notices.says: The Health Canada notice names the Anker 334 MagGo Battery, PowerCore 10K, model A1642, and says to use Anker’s site to see whether a serial number is included.
notices.howToCheck: The notice says to check the serial number on Anker’s website.
notices.remedy: The notice tells owners to stop using the product, check the serial number, and if the unit is included, dispose of it so it cannot be used again, following the municipality’s lithium-ion battery instructions.
notices.modelsLabel: Model number in this Health Canada notice

notices.title: Anker 321 Power Banks (PowerCore 5K) recalled due to potential fire hazard
notices.says: The Health Canada notice says certain units of the Anker 321 Power Bank, PowerCore 5K, black, model A1112011, are identified by specific 16-digit serial numbers on the bottom.
notices.howToCheck: The notice says the serial number is on the bottom and to check it with Anker at anker.com/ca/a1112-recall-form.
notices.remedy: The notice tells owners to stop using a recalled unit, dispose of it so it cannot be used, follow municipal lithium-ion battery instructions, and not put it in household garbage. It says Anker sends a new power bank to users verified as part of the recall batch.
notices.modelsLabel: Model number in this Health Canada notice

notices.title: Anker 535 Power Bank (PowerCore 20K) A1366 recalled due to fire hazard
notices.says: The Health Canada notice names the Anker 535 Power Bank, PowerCore 20K, model A1366, and describes a fire hazard.
notices.howToCheck: The notice names model A1366. Use the linked notice for the label details it prints.
notices.remedy: The notice tells owners to stop using the recalled power bank and contact Anker customer support for a refund.
notices.modelsLabel: Model number in this Health Canada notice

title: Vitamix Ascent and Venturist container recall, and the E310
description: The June 20, 2024 CPSC notice covers Ascent and Venturist 8-ounce and 20-ounce blending containers and blade bases. The E310 card lists an Explorian blender with a 48 oz container.
catalogue: The E310 card is the Explorian blender. Its maker-sourced spec line says the container is 48 oz. The 2024 CPSC notice names 8-ounce and 20-ounce Ascent and Venturist containers, not an Explorian E310.

notices.title: Vitamix Reannounces and Expands Recall of Ascent Series and Venturist Series 8-ounce and 20-ounce Blending Containers and Blade Bases
notices.says: The CPSC notice says the recall involves all Ascent and Venturist Series 8-ounce blending containers, 20-ounce blending containers, and blade bases, including containers repaired in the August 2018 recall. It says the clear containers and black blade bases came with certain Venturist and Ascent blenders and were also sold separately. It names the Venturist V1200 and the Ascent A2300, A2500, A3300, and A3500 as examples. It says the Vitamix logo is printed on the container.
notices.howToCheck: The notice identifies the recalled parts as Ascent and Venturist 8-ounce and 20-ounce containers and their blade bases, including units already repaired in 2018.
notices.remedy: The notice tells owners, including people who took part in the 2018 recall, to stop using the recalled 8-ounce and 20-ounce containers and blade bases and contact Vitamix for a repair kit with a protective plastic shroud and additional labels.
notices.modelsLabel: Names in the 2024 CPSC notice

notices.title: Vitamix Recalls Ascent and Venturist Series Blending Containers Due to Laceration Hazard
notices.says: The 2018 CPSC notice, which the 2024 notice expands, covered Ascent and Venturist 8-ounce and 20-ounce containers with blade date codes of March 2018 (03-18) or earlier. It says a green or orange dot on the bottom of the blade base means that container was already repaired under that recall.
notices.howToCheck: The notice says the blade date code is laser-etched on the top of the blade in the blade base, in MM-YY form.
notices.remedy: That notice told owners to stop using the recalled containers and contact Vitamix for a free repair kit. The 2024 notice above is the later instruction, including for people who already received the 2018 repair.
notices.modelsLabel: Names in the 2018 CPSC notice
models: Ascent 8-ounce containers with blade date code 03-18 or earlier
Ascent 20-ounce containers with blade date code 03-18 or earlier
Venturist 8-ounce containers with blade date code 03-18 or earlier
Venturist 20-ounce containers with blade date code 03-18 or earlier

notices.title: Vitamix Recalls 64-Ounce Low Profile Blender Container Due to Laceration Hazard
notices.says: A separate 2013 CPSC notice covers the Vitamix 64-ounce Low-Profile container with blade part number 103208 A and blade date codes 03-12 through 07-13. It names blender models 7500, Professional Series 300, and Professional Series 750. It says replacement blades with part number 104602 A are not included.
notices.howToCheck: The notice says the blade part number and date code are laser-etched on the top of the blade at the bottom of the container.
notices.remedy: The notice tells owners to stop using the recalled container and contact Vitamix for a free repair.
notices.modelsLabel: Names in the 2013 CPSC notice

notices.title: Vitamix 2-Litre (64-Ounce) Low-Profile Blender Container
notices.says: The Health Canada record dated 2013-08-28 names the Vitamix 2-litre (64-ounce) Low-Profile blender container. It is a different notice from the 2024 CPSC Ascent and Venturist container notice.
notices.howToCheck: Use the linked Health Canada notice for the container it describes.
notices.remedy: Follow the steps printed on the linked Health Canada notice.
notices.modelsLabel: Name in the Health Canada notice

title: Instant Pot official notices: Smart, Smart-60, and Gem 65
description: Official CPSC and Health Canada notices name Instant Pot Smart, Smart-60, and Gem 65 multicookers. They do not name the Duo Plus. The Duo Plus card has no matching recall record as of the catalogue check date.
catalogue: The catalogue card is the Instant Pot Duo Plus, 6 quart. Duo Plus is not a model name in the notices below.

notices.title: Instant Pot Pressure Cookers Recalled by Double Insight Due to Shock Hazard
notices.says: The CPSC notice says the recall involves Instant Pot Smart and Smart-60 electric pressure cookers. It says they are stainless steel with black plastic attachments, about 12 inches in diameter and 12 inches tall, with Instant Pot and Smart printed on the front of the control panel. It says serial numbers between 1410 and 1503 and manufacture dates between December 1, 2014 and June 1, 2015 are included.
notices.howToCheck: The notice says the serial number and date are printed on a label on the bottom of the base.
notices.remedy: The notice tells owners to stop using the recalled cooker and contact Instant Pot for a free replacement base, which is the bottom of the cooker including the control panel.
notices.modelsLabel: Models in this CPSC notice

notices.title: Double Insight Inc. recalls Instant Pot Smart Pressure Cooker
notices.says: The Health Canada notice says date codes between October 2014 (1410) and March 2015 (1503) are affected. It says those date codes are the first four digits of a longer serial number on the bottom of the base, and that the model name Smart-60 is on a label on the back of the unit.
notices.howToCheck: The notice says to read the first four digits of the serial number on the bottom, and the Smart-60 name on the back label.
notices.remedy: The notice tells owners to stop using the product and contact Double Insight for a replacement or refund.
notices.modelsLabel: Names in this Health Canada notice

notices.title: Double Insight Recalls Multicookers Due to Fire Hazard; Sold Exclusively at Walmart
notices.says: The CPSC notice says the recall involves Gem 65 8-in-1 multicookers sold exclusively at Walmart. It says Instant Pot is printed on the front, and Gem 65 8-in-1 plus a batch code of 1728, 1730, 1731, 1734, or 1746 is printed on the rating label on the underside.
notices.howToCheck: The notice says to read the underside rating label for Gem 65 8-in-1 and one of those batch codes.
notices.remedy: The notice tells owners to stop using the recalled multicooker, unplug it, and return it to Walmart for a free replacement.
notices.modelsLabel: Names in this CPSC notice

title: Lasko heater recalls: official model numbers
description: CPSC heater notices name specific older Lasko and Air King model numbers. CT32150 and CT14401 are not those model numbers. The catalogue check found no matching recall for either card on the check date.
catalogue: The catalogue heaters are CT32150 and CT14401. Neither model number is in the CPSC lists copied below.

notices.title: Lasko Recalls Portable Electric Heaters Due To Fire Hazard
notices.says: The CPSC notice says the recall involves Lasko model 5540 and Air King model 8540 portable electric tower heaters manufactured in 2002, with date codes that begin with 2. It says heaters with date codes beginning with 3, 4, or 5 are not in this recall. It describes the heaters as dark grey with silver front covers and black vent slats, 20.5 inches tall.
notices.howToCheck: The notice says the date code is a four-digit number on the label on the bottom of the unit, on the bottom left of the label, above the voltage number.
notices.remedy: The notice tells owners to stop using the heaters and contact Lasko for a free replacement heater.
notices.modelsLabel: Model numbers in this CPSC notice

notices.title: Ceramic Heaters Recalled By Lasko
notices.says: The CPSC notice says the recall involves Lasko ceramic heaters manufactured in 2005, in the model numbers listed below.
notices.howToCheck: The notice says the model number is on the bottom of the unit or at the rear of the base.
notices.remedy: The notice tells owners to stop using the heaters and contact Lasko for a free replacement heater.
notices.modelsLabel: Model numbers in this CPSC notice

notices.title: CPSC, Lasko Products Inc. Announce Recall of Space Heaters
notices.says: The CPSC notice says two heaters are in this recall. Model 5500 is an oscillating ceramic heater with dark gray vents and a bronze trim. Model 5700 is an oil-filled radiator. It says Lasko is printed near the top of both.
notices.howToCheck: The notice says the 5500 model number is on a label under the round base, and the 5700 model number is on a label on the side near the right front wheel.
notices.remedy: The notice tells owners to stop using the heaters, unplug them, and contact Lasko for instructions on returning the heater for a free replacement or a product of similar value.
notices.modelsLabel: Model numbers in this CPSC notice

title: Toro Power Clear snowblower recalls: the model numbers
description: The 2010 and 2011 CPSC and Health Canada notices name Power Clear 180 models 38272 and 38282, and PC-421 models 38588 and 38589. Catalogue model 38753 is not in those lists.
catalogue: The catalogue snow blower is Toro Power Clear 721 E, model 38753. 38753 is not among the model numbers listed above. The EGO SNT2110 and Snow Joe 24V-SS10 cards are different tools and are not named in these Toro notices.

notices.title: Snow Blowers Recalled by The Toro Company Due to Fire Hazard
notices.says: The CPSC notice says the recall involves Toro Power Clear 180 single-stage snow blowers, model numbers 38272 and 38282, serial numbers 310000001 through 310999999. It says the model and serial number are on a decal on the lower right side of the snow blower. It describes a fire hazard from a corroded carburetor needle that can stick open and leak fuel.
notices.howToCheck: The notice says to read the model and serial decal on the lower right side.
notices.remedy: The notice tells owners to stop using a unit in the recall and contact an authorized Toro service dealer for a free repair.
notices.modelsLabel: Model numbers in this CPSC notice

notices.title: Toro Power Clear 180 Snow Blower
notices.says: The Health Canada notice says the recall involves Toro Power Clear 180 single-stage snow blowers, model numbers 38272 and 38282, serial numbers 310000001 through 310999999. It says the model serial decal is on the lower right rear of the machine. It is a joint recall with the CPSC.
notices.howToCheck: The notice says the model serial decal is on the lower right rear of the machine.
notices.remedy: The notice tells owners to check whether the snow blower is included and contact an authorized Toro service dealer for a free repair.
notices.modelsLabel: Model numbers in this Health Canada notice

notices.title: Toro Recalls Power Clear Snowblowers and Recycler Mowers Due to Fire or Burn Hazard
notices.says: The CPSC notice says the snowblower recall involves Toro PC-421Q models 38588 and 38589. It lists serial ranges for each model and says the model and serial numbers are on a decal on the underside of the rear of the unit. It also names Recycler mower model 20323. It says the carburetors can leak fuel and ignite.
notices.howToCheck: The notice says the snowblower model and serial numbers are on a decal on the underside of the rear of the unit.
notices.remedy: The notice tells owners to stop using the products and contact a Toro service dealer for a free repair.
notices.modelsLabel: Snowblower model numbers in this CPSC notice

notices.title: Toro Power Clear Snow Blower and Push Recycler Mower
notices.says: The Health Canada notice says the recall involves 2010 and 2011 Toro Power Clear 421Q snow blowers. It names model 38588 with serials 310000001 to 311003576, and model 38589 with serials 310000001 to 311999999. It also names push mower model 20323. It says the snow blower model and serial numbers are on a decal on the underside of the rear of the unit.
notices.howToCheck: The notice says to read the decal on the underside of the rear of the snow blower.
notices.remedy: The notice tells owners to stop using the snow blowers and mowers and contact a Toro service dealer for a free repair.
notices.modelsLabel: Snowblower model numbers in this Health Canada notice

title: Shark Rotator Lift-Away recall: the 2015 model numbers
description: CPSC names NV650W, NV651, NV652, and NV660. Health Canada names NV650W and NV652. AV2501S, AV2820AE, and IP3251 are not those models.
catalogue: The catalogue Shark cards are AV2501S, AV2820AE, and IP3251. None of those model numbers is among the 2015 models listed above.

notices.title: Shark Vacuum Cleaners Recalled by Euro-Pro
notices.says: The CPSC notice says the recall involves four models of Shark Rotator Powered Lift-Away upright vacuum cleaners: NV650W, NV651, NV652, and NV660. It says the model number is on a silver sticker on the upper right-hand corner of the back of the unit. It says recalled units have a date code on the power-plug prong beginning with 48 or lower and ending with 14, in WWYY form. It says units marked with a dimple or a green circle sticker on the plastic cuff that holds the aluminum wand were inspected and are not included. It describes an electric-shock hazard if the aluminum wand disconnects and stays energized.
notices.howToCheck: The notice says to read the model sticker on the back, the date code on the plug prong, and whether the cuff has a dimple or a green circle sticker.
notices.remedy: The notice tells owners to stop using the recalled vacuum cleaners and contact Euro-Pro for a free replacement wand.
notices.modelsLabel: Model numbers in this CPSC notice

notices.title: Euro-Pro Operating LLC recalls Shark brand vacuum cleaners
notices.says: The Health Canada notice says the recall involves certain Shark Rotator Powered Lift-Away upright vacuum cleaners and names models NV650W and NV652. It says the model number is on a silver sticker on the upper right-hand corner of the back. It uses the same date-code rule, codes beginning with 48 or lower and ending with 14, and the same dimple or green-circle exclusion. It is a joint recall with the CPSC. The CPSC notice also names NV651 and NV660, which this Health Canada model table does not list.
notices.howToCheck: The notice says to read the model sticker, the date code on the plug prong, and the cuff mark.
notices.remedy: The notice tells owners to stop using the recalled vacuum cleaners and contact Euro-Pro for a free replacement wand.
notices.modelsLabel: Model numbers in this Health Canada notice

title: Air fryer recalls: what owners should know
description: These are the air fryer notices on file from CPSC and Health Canada. They cover Cosori, Gourmia, Insignia, PowerXL, Secura, and Ninja Foodi OP300, with the hazard, what owners should do, and the model numbers.
tableHeading: Ninja, Cosori, and the other air fryer notices
catalogue: The COSORI Pro II card’s capacity line is 5.8 qt, and the model string used on its explainer is the CS358-AF series. CS358-AF is not in the Cosori model list below. The Foodi 10-in-1 card is an oven function list, not an OP300 model number. The Crispi card’s modes include Air Fry, and FN101 is not in the OP300 list. Match the number on the unit to the number in the notice.

notices.title: Two Million COSORI Air Fryers Recalled by Atekcity Due to Fire and Burn Hazards
notices.hazard: The notice says a wire connection in the air fryers can overheat, posing fire and burn hazards.
notices.says: The CPSC notice, recall number 23-130, says this recall involves Cosori air fryers in the model numbers listed below. It says the brand name Cosori is on the front, and the model number is printed on the bottom label and in the user manual. It says the units are 3.7 and 5.8 quart, sold in black, gray, white, blue, or red. It says about 2 million were recalled, and about 250,000 were sold in Canada and about 21,000 in Mexico. The Health Canada notice below prints different unit figures. It says the firm has received 205 reports of the air fryers catching fire, burning, melting, overheating, and smoking, including 10 reports of minor superficial burn injuries and 23 reports of minor property damage.
notices.howToCheck: The notice says to read the model number on the bottom label of the unit and in the user manual.
notices.remedy: The notice tells owners to stop using the recalled air fryers and contact Cosori for a free replacement air fryer or another Cosori product. It says registration asks for contact information and photos of the unit with the cord cut, and that no receipt is needed.
notices.modelsLabel: Model numbers in the CPSC notice

notices.title: Certain models of Cosori-branded Air Fryers recalled due to potential fire hazard
notices.hazard: The notice says the wire connectors can overheat, posing a potential burn and fire hazard.
notices.says: The Health Canada notice, updated 2023-02-23, identification RA-72618, says the recall involves certain Cosori-branded air fryers. It says the model number is on the bottom label and in the user manual, and the batch number is on the bottom or at the back below the rear exhaust vent. It says the company reported 252,828 units sold in Canada, 2,042,631 in the United States, and 21,490 in Mexico, sold from March 2019 to December 2022. Those unit figures are not the same figures as the CPSC notice’s “about 2 million” and “about 250,000” in Canada. It says that as of February 2023 the company had received 205 reports globally, including 56 in Canada, of the air fryers catching fire, burning, melting, overheating, and smoking, with 10 reports of minor superficial burn injuries including 4 in Canada, and 23 reports of minor property damage globally. It says the notice is a joint recall with the CPSC.
notices.howToCheck: The notice says the model number is on the bottom label and in the user manual, and the batch number is on the bottom of the unit or at the back below the rear exhaust vent.
notices.remedy: The notice tells owners to stop using the recalled products immediately and contact Cosori for a replacement unit. It says no receipt is needed, and it names registration at the Cosori recall page or the recall hotline.
notices.modelsLabel: Model numbers in the Health Canada notice

notices.title: Gourmia Recalls 9-Slice Digital Air Fryer Ovens Due to Burn Hazard
notices.hazard: The notice says the oven’s doors can unexpectedly close when bumped, posing a burn hazard to consumers retrieving hot food.
notices.says: The CPSC notice, recall number 27-069, dated November 05, 2026, says this recall involves Gourmia stainless steel digital 9-slice air fryer ovens, model GTF7530, UPC 810002862779. It says the ovens have two spring-loaded glass front French doors with metal handles. It says model GTF7530 and codes 3021 to 0126 can be found on a label on the back of the unit. It says about 175,951 units. It says Gourmia has received 57 reports of the doors closing unexpectedly when retrieving food, resulting in 40 incidents of burns to hands or wrists.
notices.howToCheck: The notice says the model and UPC are on the packaging, and model GTF7530 and codes 3021 to 0126 are on a label on the back of the unit.
notices.remedy: The notice tells owners to stop using the ovens immediately and contact Gourmia for a free repair kit by mail. It says the kit includes an added doorstop and installation instructions.
notices.modelsLabel: Model number in the CPSC notice

notices.product: Insignia air fryers and air fryer ovens
notices.title: Best Buy Recalls Insignia Air Fryers and Air Fryer Ovens Due to Fire, Burn and Laceration Hazards
notices.hazard: The notice says the air fryers can overheat, causing the handles to melt or break, posing fire and burn hazards, and that the air fryer ovens can overheat and the glass on the door can shatter, posing fire, burn, and laceration hazards.
notices.says: The CPSC notice, recall number 24-159, says this recall involves Insignia air fryers and air fryer ovens in the model numbers listed below. It says INSIGNIA is on the top or front, and a rating label on the underside identifies the brand and the model number. It says capacities range from about 3.4 to 10 quarts. It says about 187,400 units, and about 99,900 were sold in Canada. It says the firm has received 24 reports of overheating, melting, or glass shattering, including six reports of air fryers catching fire, and that no injuries or property damage have been reported.
notices.howToCheck: The notice says the model number is on the product rating label on the underside of the unit.
notices.remedy: The notice tells owners to stop using the units and follow the instructions at the Best Buy recall registration page, including photos of the unit, the model number, the purchase receipt, and the destruction of the unit. It says the refund is a refund check or a Best Buy store credit, in the amount on the receipt, or the average sales price for the model if no receipt is provided. It says not to return the units to Best Buy stores.
notices.modelsLabel: Model numbers in the CPSC notice

notices.title: Empower Brands Recalls Power XL Dual Basket Air Fryers Due to Burn Hazard
notices.hazard: The notice says the plastic U-channel connector used to combine the two baskets can break during use, posing a burn hazard.
notices.says: The CPSC notice, recall number 24-051, says this recall involves PowerXL Vortex dual-basket air fryers, models DUAF-10 and DUAF-005. It says the 10-quart DUAF-10 is about 17 inches long by 16 inches wide by 12 1/2 inches tall and weighs about 14 1/2 pounds, and the 9-quart DUAF-005 is about 14 inches long by 13 inches wide by 15 inches tall and weighs about 14 pounds. It says they were sold in black or cinnamon, with a silver PowerXL label on the front and a white label on the bottom or on the power cord that lists the model number. It says about 319,000 units. It says the firm has received 41 reports of the product breaking during use, including three reports of burns.
notices.howToCheck: The notice says the model number is on a white label on the bottom of the unit or on the power cord.
notices.remedy: The notice tells owners to stop using the recalled dual-basket air fryers immediately and contact Empower Brands for a full refund.
notices.modelsLabel: Model numbers in the CPSC notice

notices.title: Secura Recalls Air Fryers Due to Fire and Burn Hazards
notices.hazard: The notice says a wire connection in the air fryer can overheat, posing fire and burn hazards.
notices.says: The CPSC notice, recall number 23-794, says this recall involves Secura air fryers, model SAF-53D (TXG-DT16E) with date code 1901, and model SAF-53 (TXG-DS16) with date codes 1903 and 1904. It says they are black with a silver accent, Secura is on the top, and the model number and four-digit date code are on silver labels at the bottom. It says they measure about 12 inches high, 11 inches deep, and 12 inches wide. It says about 6,400 units, and about 680 were sold in Canada. It says the firm has received nine reports of the air fryers catching fire, burning, and smoking, and that no injuries or property damage have been reported. The Health Canada notice below is narrower: it names only SAF-53 (TXG-DS16) with date codes 1903 and 1904.
notices.howToCheck: The notice says the model number and the four-digit date code are on the silver labels at the bottom of the unit.
notices.remedy: The notice tells owners to stop using the recalled air fryers and contact Secura. It says registration asks for contact information, photos of the unit with the power cord cut, and the date code. It says no receipt is needed to receive a replacement. It also names an Amazon gift card. The amount is printed on the CPSC notice, which is linked here.
notices.modelsLabel: Model numbers in the CPSC notice

notices.title: Secura Air Fryers recalled due to fire and burn hazards
notices.hazard: The notice says a wire connection in the air fryer can overheat, posing fire and burn hazards.
notices.says: The Health Canada notice, updated 2026-05-22, identification RA-82098, says this recall involves Secura air fryers with model number SAF-53 (TXG-DS16) only, with date codes 1903 and 1904. It does not name SAF-53D or date code 1901. It says they are black with a silver accent, Secura is on the top, and the model number and date code are on silver labels at the bottom. It says they measure about 30 cm high, 28 cm deep, and 30 cm wide. It says 680 units were sold in Canada from May 2019 to October 2020. It says that as of May 14, 2026, the company had received no reports of incident or injury in Canada.
notices.howToCheck: The notice says the model number and the four-digit date code are printed on the silver labels at the bottom of the unit.
notices.remedy: The notice tells owners to stop using the recalled product and contact Secura for an Amazon.ca gift card code. It says valid proof of purchase is required, and it points owners to the company’s recall instructions.
notices.modelsLabel: Model number in the Health Canada notice

notices.product: Ninja Foodi OP300 series pressure cookers
notices.title: SharkNinja Recalls Foodi Multi-Function Pressure Cookers Due to Burn Hazard
notices.hazard: The notice says the pressure-cooking lid can be opened during use, causing hot contents to escape, posing a risk of burn injuries.
notices.says: The CPSC notice, recall number 25-247, says this recall involves all Ninja Foodi OP300 Series multi-function pressure cookers. It says the cookers have functions that include pressure cooking and air frying, were sold in black, and have a 6.5-quart capacity. It says Ninja is printed on the front and on the product label. It says an extra code after the model number is not part of the model designation, and gives the example that a unit labeled OP301 I07 is a model OP301. It says replacement pressure-cooker lids bought as a separate part are included. It says about 1,846,400 units, and about 184,240 were sold in Canada. It says SharkNinja has received 106 reports of burn injuries, including more than 50 reports of second- or third-degree burns, with 26 lawsuits filed. This is a pressure-cooking lid notice. It is not a notice for the NC301 ice cream maker or for the Crispi FN101.
notices.howToCheck: The notice says the model numbers are printed on a label on the side of the cooker.
notices.remedy: The notice tells owners to stop using the pressure-cooking function and contact SharkNinja for a free replacement lid. It says the air frying and other functions can still be used.
notices.modelsLabel: Model numbers in the CPSC notice

title: Space heater recalls: what owners should know
description: These are the space heater notices on file from CPSC and Health Canada. They cover Vornado, Lasko, DREO, Govee, and One Stop Gardens, with the hazard, what owners should do, and the model numbers.
tableHeading: Lasko heater recalls and the other notices
catalogue: The catalogue heaters on this page are CT32150, CT14401, the Dreo Atom 316, and the Vornado AVH2. CT32150 and CT14401 are not in the Lasko model lists below. The Atom 316 is not DR-HSH015. The AVH2 is not TYPE SRTH, TYPE VH2, or the VH110 serial pattern. Read the model on the unit before applying a notice.

notices.title: Vornado Air Recalls SRTH Small Room Tower Heaters Due to Fire Hazard
notices.hazard: The notice says the fan blade can detach from the motor shaft, which can cause the fan to slow or stop, leading to overheating, melting, and a fire hazard if the thermal cutoff or fuse does not activate in time.
notices.says: The CPSC notice, recall number 26-532, says the recalled Vornado SRTH small room tower heaters were sold in black and white and measure about 12.5 inches high by 6 inches in diameter. It says they have two heat settings and a fan-only setting. It says TYPE SRTH is printed on the silver rating label on the bottom. It says about 255,000 units, and about eight were sold in Canada. It says Vornado has received 32 reports of overheating from fan displacement, including eight reports of fire and one report of smoke inhalation.
notices.howToCheck: The notice says TYPE SRTH is on the silver rating label on the bottom of the heater.
notices.remedy: The notice tells owners to stop using the heaters immediately and contact Vornado for instructions on submitting photos of the product and proof of destruction to receive a full refund.
notices.modelsLabel: Model line in the CPSC notice

notices.title: Vornado Air Recalls VH2 Whole Room Heaters Due to Electric Shock and Fire Hazards
notices.hazard: The notice says the power cord can partially detach from the heater enclosure, which can lead to cord damage over time, posing electric shock and fire hazards.
notices.says: The CPSC notice, recall number 25-093, says the recall involves Vornado VH2 whole room heaters with a JUL24 or AUG24 date code and TYPE VH2 on the silver rating label on the underside. It says only those date codes are included. It says the heaters are off white, with thermostatic control, automatic or continuous fan operation, and two heat settings. It says about 7,780 units. It says no incidents were reported.
notices.howToCheck: The notice says TYPE VH2 and the JUL24 or AUG24 date code are on the silver rating label on the underside.
notices.remedy: The notice tells owners to stop using the recalled heaters and contact Vornado to confirm the unit is included and to receive instructions for a free replacement heater.
notices.modelsLabel: Model line in the CPSC notice
models: TYPE VH2 with date code JUL24 or AUG24

notices.title: Vornado Air Recalls Electric Space Heaters
notices.hazard: The notice says the heater can overheat and cause the units to melt, catch fire, and ignite nearby items, posing a fire and burn hazard.
notices.says: The CPSC notice, recall number 14-256, says this recall involves Vornado VH110 whole room vortex heaters in black and white. It says recalled heaters have the numbers 1 and 3 as the fourth and fifth digits of the serial number, on a silver decal on the bottom. It says the heaters measure about 10.5 inches high, 9 inches deep, and 10.5 inches at the base. It says about 79,000 units. It says Vornado has received 29 reports of units overheating and melting, including seven reports of heaters catching fire, one report of smoke inhalation, and one report of property damage from soot and smoke.
notices.howToCheck: The notice says the model and serial numbers are on a silver decal on the bottom, and that recalled units have 1 and 3 as the fourth and fifth serial digits.
notices.remedy: The notice tells owners to turn the heater off, unplug it, and contact Vornado for a free replacement unit, including free shipping.
notices.modelsLabel: Model line in the CPSC notice
models: VH110 with serial digits 1 and 3 in the fourth and fifth places

notices.title: Lasko Recalls Portable Electric Heaters Due To Fire Hazard
notices.hazard: The notice says an electrical connection in the base can overheat, causing it to melt and expose the electrical connection, posing a fire hazard.
notices.says: The CPSC notice, release 11-121, says the recall involves Lasko model 5540 and Air King model 8540 portable electric tower heaters manufactured in 2002, with date codes that begin with 2. It says heaters with date codes beginning with 3, 4, or 5 are not in this recall. It says the heaters are 20.5 inches tall, dark grey with silver front covers and black vent slats. It says about 107,500 units. It says Lasko received 36 reports of the connection overheating, with no reports of injury, and 18 reports of minor burn damage to floors or carpets. A note on the page says the firm’s recall hotline number has changed.
notices.howToCheck: The notice says the date code is a four-digit number on the label on the bottom of the unit, on the bottom left of the label, above the voltage number.
notices.remedy: The notice tells owners to stop using the heaters immediately and contact Lasko for a free replacement heater.
notices.modelsLabel: Model numbers in the CPSC notice

notices.title: Ceramic Heaters Recalled By Lasko
notices.hazard: The notice says the heater’s cord can overheat where it enters the base, which could pose a fire hazard.
notices.says: The CPSC notice, recall number 07-227, says the recall involves Lasko ceramic heaters manufactured in 2005, in the model numbers listed below. It says about 1.2 million units. It says Lasko has received 28 reports of failed power cords, including six reports of minor property damage, and that no injuries have been reported. A note on the page says the firm contact number and website changed.
notices.howToCheck: The notice says the model number is on the bottom of the unit or at the rear of the base.
notices.remedy: The notice tells owners to stop using the heaters immediately and contact Lasko for a free replacement heater.
notices.modelsLabel: Model numbers in the CPSC notice

notices.title: CPSC, Lasko Products Inc. Announce Recall of Space Heaters
notices.hazard: The notice says the power cord connection can overheat and cause the cord to separate from the heater, posing a fire, burn, and shock hazard.
notices.says: The CPSC notice, recall number 04-094, says two heaters are in this recall. It says model 5500 is an oscillating ceramic heater with dark grey vents and a bronze trim, and model 5700 is an oil-filled radiator. It says Lasko is printed near the top of both. It says 186,000 units. It says four consumers reported burned and detached power cords, and that no injuries were reported.
notices.howToCheck: The notice says the 5500 model number is on a label under the round base, and the 5700 model number is on a label on the side near the right front wheel.
notices.remedy: The notice tells owners to stop using the heaters, unplug them, and contact Lasko for instructions on returning the heater for a free replacement or a product of similar value.
notices.modelsLabel: Model numbers in the CPSC notice

notices.title: DREO Space Heaters recalled due to fire and burn hazards
notices.hazard: The notice says the recalled space heaters can overheat and ignite, posing fire and burn hazards.
notices.says: The Health Canada notice, updated 2026-10-29, identification RA-82854, says the recall involves DREO portable oscillating ceramic space heaters, model DR-HSH015. It says affected units were manufactured from April 2025 (2025/04) to January 2026 (2026/01). It says the heaters are black, about 29 cm wide by 33 cm tall, and include a remote control. It says 36,288 units were sold in Canada and 338,800 in the United States, from September 2025 to August 2026. It says that as of October 22, 2026, the company had received one reported incident and no reports of injury in Canada, and 16 reports of incidents with one report of injury in the United States. It says the notice is a joint recall with the CPSC. The Atom 316 card is a different model string.
notices.howToCheck: The notice says the model number and the manufacture date are on labels on the underside.
notices.remedy: The notice tells owners to stop using the recalled product immediately and contact DREO for a free replacement space heater.
notices.modelsLabel: Model number in the Health Canada notice

notices.title: GoveeLife and Govee Smart Electric Space Heaters recalled due to fire hazard
notices.hazard: The notice says the products can overheat, posing fire and burn hazards.
notices.says: The Health Canada notice, updated 2024-11-07, identification RA-76452, says the recall involves GoveeLife and Govee smart electric space heaters in the model numbers listed below, including the H7130101 variation of H7130. It says the brand is on the front or side, the heaters were sold in black and white, and height runs from 9 inches to 26 inches depending on the model. It says approximately 48,584 units were sold in Canada. It also prints a United States count on the same page. It says that as of October 28, 2024, the company had received 7 reports of overheating in Canada and no report of injuries, and 106 reports of overheating and one report of a minor burn injury in the United States. It says the notice is a joint recall with the CPSC.
notices.howToCheck: The notice says the model number is on the manufacturer’s label on the underside of the unit.
notices.remedy: The notice tells owners to stop using the recalled heaters and register at the GoveeLife heater recall page for a refund.
notices.modelsLabel: Model numbers in the Health Canada notice

notices.product: One Stop Gardens tank-top propane heaters
notices.title: Harbor Freight Tools Recalls One Stop Gardens Tank Top Propane Heaters Due to Burn Hazard
notices.hazard: The notice says that in windy weather the flame can be directed to the rear and can melt the tip-switch safety shutoff, so the heater may not turn off if it tips over, posing a burn hazard.
notices.says: The CPSC notice, recall number 21-168, says this recall involves the One Stop Gardens 15,000 BTU tank-top propane heater, item 63073, and the 30,000 BTU heater, item 63072. It says the heaters mount on a standard 20 lb propane tank. It says about 350,000 units. It says the firm has received nine reports of flame redirection or a melted tip switch, and that three incidents resulted in minor burn injuries when consumers tried to turn the unit off. These item numbers are not the catalogue heater model numbers.
notices.howToCheck: The notice says item 63073 is on the hang tag of the 15,000 BTU heater and item 63072 is on the label of the 30,000 BTU heater.
notices.remedy: The notice tells owners to stop using the heaters and return them to a Harbor Freight Tools store for a refund of the purchase price, plus applicable tax, as a Harbor Freight Tools gift card. It says Harbor Freight is contacting known purchasers.
notices.modelsLabel: Item numbers in the CPSC notice
